main_text.head: QVVM ALIOQVI VACATVRAE essent hę pagines, adiunxi memorabilem illam famem quam Eusebeb. lib.9.cap.8. describit.
main_text.p: SVb imperio Maximini & Licinij persequtorū Christianæ religionis, fames fuit tāta, ut ūna tritici mēsura bis mille et quingentis Atticis venderetur. Factum inde est, ut per ciuitates infinita hominū multitudo fame cōsecta, mortua sit: maior vero ꝑ vicos & agros pestileti[?] morbo: Alij vero quæ charissima & pretiosissima haberent pro tenuis-simo cibo ditioribus vendebant: alij possessionibus suis paulatim diuenditis, ad extremā egestatem redacti sunt. Quidā modicas graminis minutias mandentes, & lethiferis herbis promiscuò vescentes, valetudinem corruperunt. Nonnullæ etiam per ciuitates nobiles fœminæ adextremam inopiā redactæ, ad agros mendicandi gratia se receperunt. Et alij quidem viribus exhausti, velut examina simulachra, huc illuc vacillantes, nutantesq; et collabantes in medijs plateis pro-cidebant:

page.notes: Heading "Eusebs." is printed with a full stop after a short word; read as "Eusebeb." — the letters are unclear, so it is doubtful. Check against the scan. The first word of the body is a large initial: "SVb" joined to the S of "Sub". "pestileti" is doubtful; it may be a printing error for "pestilenti" or "pestilētī". Marked [?]. A small mark (possibly a reference sign or signature-like figure) stands between "nutantesq;" and "et" on the scan; not transcribed as text. The line "cidebant:" is right-aligned as the end of the paragraph; the word is split across lines as "pro=" / "cidebant:", transcribed with a printed hyphen. Show-through from the other side is faint at the top and is left out.
